subject: Private hosting addendum — redlines & evidence delivery timeline
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediq.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, procurement@mediq.com
Cc: Tom Gallagher <tgallagher@mediq.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting addendum — initial redlines and evidence ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are the initial redlines from our legal and procurement teams (MediQ_PrivateAddendum_Redlines_v1.pdf) and an operator runbook template they asked us to fill out. High level asks from our side:

- Narrow the license footprint to the single app bundle we listed in the Order Form (section 2.1).
- Clarify the operator access window for forensic snapshots and include a list of expected artifacts.
- A short escrow-lite path if Redwood cannot meet the operator runbook witness in our region within 60 days.
- A revised timeline for executing any MSA addendum + Order Form signoff (we are planning a procurement review on 7/20).

Can you confirm who on your side will own the runbook and the redline responses? Also please flag anything you see as a hard stop from your security/compliance side.

We want to avoid a long legal back-and-forth — if you can provide a proposed timeline for redline resolution and evidence delivery that would help our procurement cadence.

Thanks,

Lara Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
MediQ Health

Attachments: MediQ_PrivateAddendum_Redlines_v1.pdf, Operator_Runbook_SOW.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediq.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting addendum — initial redlines and evidence ask

Hi Lara — thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- We will treat the license scope change as a high-priority redline. Redwood can accept restricting the licensed bundle to the named application, subject to a tight definition in exhibit A.
- Priyom (cc'd) will lead the redline responses and coordinate legal with your counsel.
- Vivek (cc'd) will coordinate the operational evidence and schedule the witness/runbook review.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- By 7/14: Redwood sends consolidated redline responses + a focused exhibit A draft.
- By 7/18: Operational evidence checklist and three proposed windows for witness/runbook walkthrough (one of which will be within 30 days).
- By 7/20: We aim to have a version of the addendum that both sides can present to procurement.

We do want to avoid an open-ended escrow requirement. We can offer an "escrow-lite" alternative: a sealed snapshot deposit with a defined access playbook that requires joint attestation and a narrow forensics scope. Priyom will include suggested guardrails (who can trigger access, retention limits, etc.).

I'll follow up internally right after this to align legal + ops. If procurement needs anything before the 7/20 review, let me know.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediq.com>, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood redline responses + evidence checklist (draft)

Hi Lara — attached is our working draft of the MSA addendum and a redline PDF (Redwood_MSA_Addendum_DRAFT.docx). Key points called out in the draft:

1) License scope: we accept an app-scoped license as proposed, provided the exhibit A defines the package by repository/artifact IDs and a short list of permitted integrations. This avoids ambiguity if you add connectors later.

2) Operator access & snapshots: we propose a limited witness window model:
   - Redwood provides a 4-hour remote witness session for a forensic snapshot within a 60-day window after go-live (two discretionary windows if mutually agreed).
   - Access to artifacts will be limited to the manifests, environment variables (redacted), and a read-only copy of the runtime image.

3) Escrow-lite:
   - If Redwood cannot provide the witness within 60 days, we will deposit a sealed snapshot with an approved third-party custodian.
   - Access to the custodian will require a joint 2-person attestation and a scoped trigger (bankruptcy, material breach, or agreed termination).
   - We are not comfortable with a broad access governance model; triggers and retention must be explicit.

4) Evidence delivery timeline:
   - By 7/18: Ops checklist and three candidate witness dates.
   - By 7/19: Legal redline table with line-item rationale (we will call out any absolute no-go clauses).

Open items for your counsel to confirm: acceptable triggers for custodian access, required attestations for runbook witness, and whether your procurement needs any additional indemnity carveouts.

Please review the attached redline and the proposed custody guardrails. If acceptable, we will produce a clean addendum for signature and prepare the operator runbook session workbook.

Thanks,

Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Addendum_DRAFT.docx

From: Tom Gallagher <tgallagher@mediq.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediq.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting addendum — initial redlines and evidence ask

Olga / Priyom — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the practical escrow-lite proposal. A few follow-ups from our legal/procurement team after a quick pass:

- We like the app-scoped license approach; please include the artifact list as a table in Exhibit A so procurement has a clear checklist.
- For the sealed snapshot, can you add a maximum retention period (we suggest 12 months) and a one-time verification drill at deposit to confirm integrity?
- Procurement would like to see the custody third party (name + SLA) or a short list of acceptable custodians before signing.

Next steps: we will circulate the attachments internally and aim to confirm procurement feedback by 7/19 EOD. If all aligns, we can move to DocuSign the addendum the following week.

Appreciate the clear timeline — this helps our 7/20 procurement review.

Best,

Tom Gallagher
Director, Strategic Procurement
MediQ Health

Attachments: none
